Yeast is a type of fungus that plays a crucial role in various fermentation processes, including those used in natural farming practices. It is a single-celled microorganism that belongs to the kingdom Fungi and is known for its ability to convert sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide through the process of fermentation. This ability makes yeast invaluable in the production of bread, beer, wine, and other fermented products.

In the context of natural farming, as described in the provided text, yeast contributes to the production of hormones during the fermentation process. These hormones include auxins, gibberellins, and cytokines, which are produced by yeast and filamentous fungi. Auxins are involved in the regulation of plant growth, gibberellins play a role in stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering, while cytokines are involved in cell division and growth. The production of these hormones during fermentation can enhance plant growth and development, making fermented farming inputs like Fermented Plant Juice (FPJ) and Fish Amino Acids (FAA) highly beneficial for crops.

Yeast's role in natural farming extends beyond hormone production. It also contributes to the breakdown of organic materials, making nutrients more readily available to plants. This process improves soil fertility and promotes the development of a healthy, balanced soil ecosystem.

In summary, yeast is a vital component of natural farming practices, contributing to the fermentation of organic inputs, the production of growth-promoting hormones, and the enhancement of soil fertility and plant health. Its ability to transform simple sugars into beneficial by-products makes it an indispensable tool in the natural farmer's toolkit.
